text: These are red-flag signs that always need emergency care. A health center poster that matches official advice is a source you can trust.
Keep the nearest hospital and emergency numbers saved, and ask your health center to explain the signs.

KidneyClear Official Store
"As a doctor for 30 years, I only trust this one fruit drink. It melts kidney stones overnight. Hospitals do not want you to know!" Dr. Ernesto Malabanan-Ruiz
A made-up older doctor with a stethoscope in a video frame. The picture is synthetic.
AI can fake a doctor's face and voice. A "doctor" who appears only in a sales ad, not on their own official page, is a red flag. No drink melts kidney stones overnight.
Look for the doctor's own official page and the product on the FDA Philippines verification portal.
CONTENT_GUIDE safe facts: deepfaked doctor endorsements; villain card: Dr. Fake
Lola Ising's Herbal Corner
Page · 3h · 5.6K shares
Our 9-herb oil cures arthritis, asthma, high blood, ulcer AND cancer! 100% natural, no side effects. Order now, 3 bottles for only ₱999!
One product that cures many unrelated diseases is a classic miracle-cure claim. "Natural" does not mean safe, and no herbal oil cures cancer.
Search the product on the FDA Philippines verification portal and ask your health worker before buying.
CONTENT_GUIDE villain card: Miracle Mike; no proven herbal cure for cancer
Kuya Nards
Forwarded · San Isidro Folks GC · 2:10 PM
What hospitals won't tell you: tawa-tawa tea cures dengue in 3 days! They hide it so you get confined and pay. Share before they take it down!
There is no herbal cure for dengue, tawa-tawa included. "Hospitals are hiding it" has no evidence. Waiting on a remedy can delay care for warning signs.
Ask a health worker early if someone has a high fever, and learn the dengue warning signs from DOH.
WHO dengue fact sheet; CONTENT_GUIDE: no herbal cure for dengue; villain card: Conspiracy Kuya
Jessa Malonzo
Life hack: every time I catch a cold, I take my leftover antibiotics and I get well in 3 days. Our whole family does this, it really works!
Colds are caused by viruses, and antibiotics do not work on viruses. Colds usually get better on their own. Using leftover antibiotics helps germs become resistant.
Use antibiotics only when a health worker prescribes them. Ask at the health center for cold care tips.
WHO antimicrobial resistance fact sheet; CONTENT_GUIDE safe facts: antibiotics do not work on viruses
Nurse Edna Villareal
Public · 9h · 640 shares

A bit surprising, but true: tawa-tawa and papaya leaf are loved home remedies, but there is NO proven herbal cure for dengue. What helps is fluids and close watching by health workers. Please share in your GC!
Health authorities agree there is no herbal cure for dengue. A post can use caps and "share" and still be true; what matters is whether it matches trusted sources.
Compare it with the DOH or WHO dengue pages before you share it.
WHO dengue fact sheet; CONTENT_GUIDE safe facts: no herbal cure for dengue
Kuya Ben
Friends Since HS GC · 11:03 PM

I just noticed that the "miracle" capsules have a small "No approved therapeutic claims" note on the label. That means it is only a food supplement, not medicine. So it cannot replace your prescription.
In the Philippines, food supplements must carry the note "No approved therapeutic claims". They are not medicine and do not replace prescribed treatment.
Read the label, then look the product up on the FDA Philippines verification portal.
FDA Philippines labelling rules for food supplements; CONTENT_GUIDE safe facts
I saw a video of a doctor selling a cure. How do I know if it is real?

Videos and voices can be faked with AI, and glitches are hard to spot. Check whether the doctor posted it on their own official page, and look the product up on the FDA Philippines verification portal. A doctor selling a "miracle" product is a red flag.
Spotting fakes by looking for glitches is unreliable. Checking the source is the strong move, and this answer says exactly that.
Try it: find the doctor's official page and see if the video is there.
Tita Grace Manalastas

For those who are worried: most vaccine side effects are mild, like a sore arm or slight fever for a day or two. Serious ones are rare, and safety is still monitored after approval. Ask the health center if you have questions.
Vaccines are tested before approval and monitored after. Most side effects are mild and short. Asking a health worker is a good habit, not a sign of distrust.
Bring your questions to the barangay health center before the vaccination day.
WHO vaccine safety guidance; CONTENT_GUIDE safe facts: vaccines
Tita Mercy
Forwarded many times · Grade 3 Parents GC · 9:30 PM
ADVISORY from DOH Updates PH Official (fan page): ALL schools CLOSED tomorrow due to a deadly new virus!!! Stock up on food NOW and keep the kids home!!! Pass it on to everyone!!!
"Fan page" means it is not an official page, just a look-alike. Panic words and "pass to everyone" are signs to pause and check before forwarding.
Look for the notice on the official DOH page and ask the school directly before forwarding.
CONTENT_GUIDE: look-alike pages imitate authorities; villain card: Fear Monger
Ronnie Abesamis
Public · 6h · 1.4K shares
I tested it! Salt water gargle every hour and you will never get the flu. Our whole office did it, and nobody got sick all year! Share for awareness!
One office's story is not proof. Gargling does not stop the flu. Flu vaccines, handwashing and staying home when sick are the proven steps.
Ask your health center about flu prevention before sharing the tip.
WHO influenza fact sheet; CONTENT_GUIDE villain card: Kwento Kim
PinoyBalita24 TV
Shared video · 1.2M views
BREAKING: Health experts confirm drinking hot calamansi water every morning prevents dengue. Share to protect your family!
A made-up news anchor at a desk with a headline bar. The picture is synthetic.
BREAKING NEWS
AI can make news-style clips that look real. "Health experts" are never named, and the station is unknown. Dengue is prevented by stopping mosquito breeding and bites.
Search for the story on known news sites or fact-checkers, and follow the DOH 4S for dengue.
WHO dengue fact sheet; DOH 4S; CONTENT_GUIDE villain card: Dr. Fake
Tita Lorie
Aquino Family GC · 6:55 AM
Everyone, if you waded through the flood yesterday, get checked at the health center, especially if you have a wound on your foot. Leptospirosis spreads through flood water. Earlier is better!
Wading in flood water raises leptospirosis risk, and health workers advise a check-up after exposure. A worried auntie can be right.
Ask your barangay health center about leptospirosis after floods.
WHO leptospirosis fact sheet; DOH flood health advisories
Coughing for 2 weeks or more? Get checked for TB. TB is curable with complete treatment, and treatment is free at the health center.
A made-up barangay health center with a notice board. The picture is synthetic.
FREE
A cough of two weeks or more should be checked for TB. TB is curable when treatment is completed, and treatment is free at health centers.
Visit or call your barangay health center to ask about a TB check.
WHO tuberculosis fact sheet; DOH TB programme
Doc Ana (RHU)
Barangay Liwanag Updates GC · 4:30 PM
Yes, we tried an AI note-taker at the RHU. It drafts the visit summary, but I read and correct it before it goes into your record. I am still the one responsible.
Using AI as a helper is fine when a trained person checks the work and stays responsible for it. This is what "human in the loop" means.
You can ask your doctor how AI tools are used in your visit and who checks them.
WHO guidance on ethics and governance of AI for health (human oversight, accountability)
Public · 2d
Translation apps can help you understand a medicine leaflet in English, but sometimes the translation is wrong. For how and when to take a medicine, ask the pharmacist or your doctor, not the app.
AI translation is useful but can make mistakes. Instructions about medicine should come from a health professional.
Bring the leaflet to the pharmacy and ask them to explain it.
CONTENT_GUIDE: AI can be wrong; medicines only through health workers
Can you write a reminder text for my mom to take her maintenance medicine?
Sure! "Hi Ma, just a reminder: time to take your morning medicine. Love you!" I can help with reminders, but your mom's doctor decides which medicine she takes and when.
Drafting a friendly reminder is a task AI does well. The answer also keeps medicine decisions with the doctor.
Use AI for small helper tasks; check medicine questions with the doctor.
CONTENT_GUIDE: AI as a helper; do not change maintenance medicines without a doctor
SmartClinic Plus PH
Sponsored · 1h
Meet Dr. AI Max, the robot doctor that replaces ALL human doctors! No more consultations. Just scan your face and get your prescription in 1 minute. Licensed and 100% accurate!
No AI is a licensed doctor, and no tool is 100% accurate. A face scan cannot examine you. Calling a program "Dr." is the fake expert trick.
Get prescriptions only from a licensed health professional who has checked you.
WHO guidance on AI for health; CONTENT_GUIDE villain card: Dr. Fake
Kuya Rey
Mercado Family GC · 8:12 PM
I adjust Papa's insulin myself with an AI app, based on his sugar readings. It has been 6 months and he is fine. No need to go back to the doctor!
Six good months for one person is a story, not proof. Medicine changes must be decided by a doctor who knows the patient. An app is a tool; a person stays responsible.
Bring the app readings to Papa's doctor and let the doctor decide on any change.
CONTENT_GUIDE: do not change maintenance medicines without a doctor; villain card: Kwento Kim
Alerto Pinas Now
Page · 30m · 3.3K shares
WARNING!!! ALL nurses will be REPLACED by AI robots by December!!! Your family will be cared for by MACHINES!!! Share before this gets deleted!!!
A made-up hospital with a red warning banner. The picture is synthetic.
WARNING!!!
AI helps with some tasks, but caring for patients needs people. ALL CAPS, a deadline and "before it gets deleted" are tricks to make you share in fear.
Pause. Ask a nurse or your health center how they actually use technology.
CONTENT_GUIDE villain card: Fear Monger; WHO guidance on AI for health
Ate Pia Concepcion
PSA from your big sister: AI can now make videos and voices of real people saying things they never said. So if a "doctor" video only shows up on a sales page, check their official page first.
Videos, photos and voices can be faked with AI. Spotting glitches is unreliable, so checking the source is the best step.
Find the person's own official page and see if they posted the same thing.
CONTENT_GUIDE safe facts: AI can fake videos, photos and voices
Page · Health Month poster
Our nurse mascot was drawn with AI, and our staff checked every word. Reminder: boil drinking water after floods, and wash hands with soap.
A made-up cartoon nurse mascot waving. The picture is synthetic.
An AI picture is not automatically fake news. This one is labelled, posted by the health center, and its advice matches trusted guidance.
Judge the message and the source, not only whether AI made the picture.

Write a short post about dengue prevention for our barangay page.

Here is a draft: "Cover, clean and empty water containers every week. Dengue mosquitoes breed in clean standing water." Please check it against DOH advice before posting, and say it was drafted with AI help.
The draft matches DOH dengue advice, and the chatbot asks you to check it and label AI help. That is responsible use.
Compare AI drafts with an official source before you post them.
SugarAway Capsules PH
Sponsored · Customer story
"SugarAway Capsules normalized my sugar in 2 weeks! I stopped my insulin and I feel great." Aling Nena, 68, Barangay Masagana
A made-up smiling older woman holding a capsule bottle. The picture is synthetic.
REAL REVIEW
Testimonial faces and voices can be made with AI, and one story is not proof anyway. Stopping insulin without a doctor is dangerous.
Look the product up on the FDA Philippines verification portal and ask your doctor first.
Ate Lani
Forwarded · Neighborhood GC · 11:47 PM
[Voice message 0:42] Listen, this is from a nurse at San Isidro Hospital: they say the water has bacteria, everyone is getting sick, do not go to the ER because it is full!!!
Voices can be cloned with AI, and this nurse has no name. Telling people to avoid the ER is dangerous. Strong feelings mean check first.
Check the hospital's and water district's official pages, or call them before forwarding.
CONTENT_GUIDE safe facts: voices can be faked; villain card: Fear Monger
Tita Weng
Friends · 10h
Sleep supports mood, memory and the body's defences. Teens even need more sleep than adults! So, kids, keep the phone out of the bedroom at night, okay?
Sleep supports mood, memory and the immune system, and teens need more sleep than adults. Informal advice from family can be right.
Ask your health worker how much sleep is right for each age in your family.
